current_versions.max: 26.6 shipped with Mojo 1.1 (MAX numbers separately from Mojo 1.x)
current_versions.compiler: Open source since 18 Aug 2026; external compiler contributions accepted from 1.1
current_versions.docs: Docs moved to mojolang.org (guide already uses mojolang.org links); docs.modular.com remains the MAX/Modular Cloud home

error_handling.guide_position: raises on fallible public functions, typed/domain errors preferred over bare Error, preserve cause, no catch-all success
error_handling.best_practice: 1.1 keeps def/raises semantics (fn removed in the 1.1 cleanup) and expanded error-handling docs; guide already uses def/raises/comptime/var
error_handling.evidence: Mojo v1.1.0 changelog: legacy fn/alias/__comptime_assert and @parameter if/for are gone; guide's conventions match the surviving forms

bounded_work.guide_position: Explicit budgets for inputs, buffers, queues, retries, device work, proven range arithmetic before allocation/indexing
bounded_work.best_practice: Still the correct posture; 1.x stability policy makes bounded APIs more, not less, important
bounded_work.evidence: No contradiction in 1.1 changelog; List growth fix in 1.1 does not remove caller-side allocation bounds

assertions_contracts.guide_position: debug_assert with ASSERT modes (all/safe/none/warn); dev/CI ASSERT=all, deployment at least safe; never assertion-only validation of untrusted input
assertions_contracts.best_practice: debug_assert still exists in 1.1 (its message paths were optimised and it migrated to unified closures); guide's mode policy is a project policy, not contradicted by upstream
assertions_contracts.evidence: Mojo v1.1.0 changelog mentions debug_assert in TString optimisation and unified-closure migration

memory_ownership.guide_position: Guide section 9 discusses Pointer, OwnedPointer, ArcPointer and warns against copying legacy UnsafePointer examples
memory_ownership.best_practice: 1.0 unified Pointer/UnsafePointer; 1.1 removed the pre-unification pointer aliases (MutUnsafePointer, ImmUnsafePointer, ImmutPointer, OptionalUnsafePointer etc.) in favour of MutPointer/ImmPointer/ImmOpaquePointer/OptionalPointer, removed Pointer dealloc-era APIs, and renamed OwnedPointer.steal_data/take
memory_ownership.evidence: Mojo v1.1.0 Removed section lists the removed pointer aliases and the replacement spellings, and the OwnedPointer renames

formatting.guide_position: mojo format governs; 4 spaces, 100-column target; CI gate via format + git diff rather than assuming a --check flag
formatting.best_practice: Still sound; 1.1 does not document a changed formatter contract in its changelog
formatting.evidence: No contradiction found in the 1.1 changelog fetched

static_analysis.guide_position: Guide relies on compiler diagnostics at full strength and names no Mojo language server in its toolchain workflow
static_analysis.best_practice: Mojo 1.0 shipped a new reliable LSP server and 1.1 improved LSP suggestions (e.g. off-by-one hints); a current guide should name the LSP as a paired tool like other Tiger Style guides do
static_analysis.evidence: Mojo releases page is the version authority; LSP improvements are described in the 1.0/1.1 release coverage - exact LSP feature list was not fetched from a Modular primary page in this pass, hence proposal rather than mechanical fix

concurrency.guide_position: Guide discusses asynchronous operations, cancellation and stale-result suppression generically (sections 5, 8, 11)
concurrency.best_practice: 1.1 removed the public async task API from std.runtime.asyncrt and removed AnyCoroutine/Coroutine/RaisingCoroutine from the prelude; any guidance assuming that public async surface is now dead
concurrency.evidence: Mojo v1.1.0 Removed section: async task API removed, coroutine prelude types removed

testing.guide_position: std.testing TestSuite discovered from main, run via mojo run; explicitly do not invent a mojo test command; half contract/failure-path coverage
testing.best_practice: Testing remains listed in the official Mojo docs tools/workflow index for 1.1.0; no mojo test command is documented there
testing.evidence: Mojo docs index (version 1.1.0) lists Testing under Tools & workflow

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Pin compiler+stdlib+MAX together, record build evidence, never claim a moving nightly as reproducible; header says manual reviewed 2026-09-20 identifies version 1.1.0
toolchain_pins.best_practice: Matches reality: latest stable is exactly 1.1.0 (17 Sep 2026); nightly is 1.2.0.dev2026101405 and must not be the reproducibility claim, as the guide says
toolchain_pins.evidence: Official releases page: Latest release 1.1.0 (Sep 17, 2026); nightly Oct 14, 2026 is 1.2.0.dev2026101405

security.guide_position: Python interop as trust boundary, no silent package/device/network authorisation from imports, secrets out of logs/argv/build env, reviewed install channels
security.best_practice: Strengthened, not contradicted, by 1.x: compiler is now open source and install is via uv/pixi packages per the official install page
security.evidence: Official install page for 1.1.0 installs Mojo as a Python/Conda-style package via uv or pixi

mechanical_fixes.correct: Current documentation (Mojo 1.1) uses the unified pointer family - `MutPointer`, `ImmPointer`, `ImmOpaquePointer`, `OptionalPointer` - plus `OwnedPointer` and `ArcPointer`; the pre-unification `UnsafePointer` aliases were removed in 1.1.
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Mojo v1.1.0 Removed section: removed MutUnsafePointer/ImmUnsafePointer/ImmutUnsafePointer/ImmutPointer/OptionalUnsafePointer aliases, use MutPointer/ImmPointer/ImmOpaquePointer/OptionalPointer; OwnedPointer.steal_data/take renamed to unsafe_take_allocation/into_inner

proposals.proposal: Rewrite section 9 around the 1.1 pointer taxonomy (MutPointer/ImmPointer, unsafe_ operations marking unsafety per-operation, MaybeUninit replacing UnsafeMaybeUninit, deinit() lifetime extension) and add the read -> imm argument-convention rename (read is now a hard error)
proposals.evidence: 1.1 changelog: read convention is a hard error, use imm; UnsafeMaybeUninit renamed to MaybeUninit with conformance gating; deinit() free function added
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a section-4/5/9 refresh in one pass with the mechanical fix above; re-run the reference example under 1.1.0 before claiming it compiles

proposals.proposal: Delete or re-scope every generic async/cancellation passage that assumes the removed public async task API, and state the 1.1 reality: no public std.runtime.asyncrt task API and no prelude coroutine types; cancellation guidance applies to host/device work only
proposals.evidence: 1.1 Removed section removes the async task API and AnyCoroutine/Coroutine/RaisingCoroutine
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: keep the state-machine/freshness guidance (it is host-side), remove language-async implications
